explain.say: A plastic bag, a water pipe and a fleece jumper are all made of super-long molecules. How do you build a molecule thousands of atoms long? Look at the board. You start with ethene, a small molecule called a monomer, which means one part.

explain.say: See the double bond? With heat, pressure and a catalyst, the double bond in each ethene opens into a single bond. That frees a link on each side, like hands reaching out. What do you think those free links grab?

explain.say: Other ethene molecules! Look at the chain forming. Each opened-up ethene joins the next, and the next, thousands of times. Nothing else is made; it only adds on. So we call it addition polymerisation. How many monomers do you think join?

explain.say: Thousands! Now zoom in on the board, from a shopping bag down to the chain. See the repeat unit? It is just CH2 CH2, over and over. Poly means many, so poly(ethene) means many ethenes. What would you call a polymer made from propene?

Poly(propene)! Great work. Change the monomer and you change the plastic: PVC for pipes, polystyrene for packaging. Wow: plastics last hundreds of years because microbes cannot easily break their carbon chains, so your recycling really matters.

faq.a: A monomer is a small molecule that can join with many others to make a polymer. Ethene is the monomer for poly(ethene).
A polymer is a very long molecule made of many monomers joined in a chain. Plastics, rubber, wool and DNA are all polymers.
The C=C double bond in each monomer opens up, and the monomers join end to end into a long chain. No other product forms.

faq.q: Why are plastics hard to get rid of?
faq.a: Most plastics are not biodegradable: microbes cannot easily break their strong carbon-carbon chains. They can last hundreds of years in landfill or the sea.

faq.q: How do you name a polymer?
faq.a: Put poly in front of the monomer name, in brackets: ethene makes poly(ethene), propene makes poly(propene), and chloroethene makes poly(chloroethene), known as PVC.

facts: Poly(ethene) is made by addition polymerisation of ethene monomers.
In addition polymerisation, the polymer is the only product.

quiz.why: The polymer is named after its monomer: propene.
